item.content:encoded:
Carroll batted seventh in Friday's game agaisnt the Yankees because of a recent slump, Alex Weiner of Arizona Sports reports.
Carroll, who had a double and two-run home run in a 9-2 loss to New York, entered the contest batting .147 (10-for-68) with a 32.4 strikeout percentage over the previous 19 games. "Corbin's grinding right now. We all know it," manager Torey Lovullo said."Just give him a chance to catch his breath down there, take a little pressure off of him." Carroll hasn't hit lower than fifth this season and never started a game below third in 2025. It's unclear how long Lovullo will keep Carroll this low in the order, but the Diamondbacks are a better team with him in the upper half.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- It feels like the Diamondbacks’ postseason hopes are slipping away from them.
While there are still eight games left to play -- and three against the Padres who Arizona trails in the race for the No. 3 National League Wild Card spot -- the Diamondbacks need to win games, and that's something that has eluded them of late.
The loss was the third in a row for the Diamondbacks, who have dropped six of their past eight games. Arizona opened the night four games behind the Padres and five behind the Cubs and Phillies, who are tied for the NL Wild Card lead.
This game never really seemed in doubt as the Yankees jumped on Eduardo Rodriguez in the first inning for five runs. The Bronx Bombers sent nine men to the plate in the inning and drew three walks, all of which scored, as Rodriguez threw a whopping 45 pitches in the inning.
The Diamondbacks did get a spark from Corbin Carroll, whose struggles of late prompted manager Torey Lovullo to drop him to seventh in the batting order. Carroll hit a two-run homer off Gerrit Cole in the second, but it was not nearly enough.
